subtitle: How a Poet-Sultan Drew a City Around Care

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a half-built Charminar dominating the skyline of a rising city by the Musi River
panels.action: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah stands on scaffolding beside the partly built Charminar, robes stirring in the wind, as surveyors and builders trace wide avenues and foundations of mosques, gardens and a hospital around the monument.

dialogue.text: In 1591, on the banks of the Musi, Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah named a new Hyderabad and set stone, water and words to answer one question: can a city itself be an act of care?

i18n.hi: १५९१ में मूसी किनारे, मुहम्मद क़ुली क़ुतुब शाह ने नया हैदराबाद बसाया, पत्थर, पानी और शब्दों से ये सवाल रखा: क्या पूरा शहर खुद एक देखभाल बन सकता है?

panels.shot: slow push-in on a dim interior at Golconda fort, lit by oil lamps over maps and manuscripts
panels.action: A young Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, in courtly robes yet without a crown, bends over a low desk in Golconda fort, one hand on a rolled map of the Musi valley and the other on an open Dakhni poetry manuscript.

dialogue.text: In 1580, the teenager Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah took the throne of Golconda, a diamond-rich hill kingdom whose cramped fort-city pressed against stone walls and a swelling, restless people.

i18n.hi: १५८० में किशोर मुहम्मद क़ुली क़ुतुब शाह ने हीरे-समृद्ध पहाड़ी रियासत गोलकोंडा का तख़्त संभाला, जिसका तंग क़िला-शहर पत्थर की दीवारों और उफनती भीड़ से चिपका था।

panels.shot: bird's-eye wide of Golconda fort and its surrounding settlements, contrasted with open plains and the Musi far away
panels.action: From above, the rugged Golconda fort, crowded with houses inside its walls, spills into haphazard suburbs, while in the hazy distance the Musi River glints across open, uncrowded land.

dialogue.text: Chroniclers like Ferishta remembered the fort-city as a knot of steep lanes and heat, its growth hemmed by rock and rampart. Beyond, the Musi flowed over open ground, promising space and air.

i18n.hi: फ़रिश्ता जैसे इतिहासकारों ने क़िला-शहर को खड़ी गलियों और तपिश की गाँठ कहा, जिसकी बढ़त चट्टानों और बुर्जों में फँसी थी। आगे खुली ज़मीन पर मूसी बहती थी, हवा और जगह का वादा करती हुई।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Muhammad Quli seated with architects and advisors around a floor map
panels.action: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah sits cross-legged with his architects and officials around a large map laid on the floor, his finger tracing a grid on the south bank of the Musi as others lean in, listening.

dialogue.speaker: muhammad_quli_qutb_shah
dialogue.text: A new shahr must rise by the Musi—planned, wide, and full of life.

i18n.hi: मूसी किनारे नया शहर उठना था—सोचा-समझा, खुला, धड़कता हुआ।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Musi riverbank at dawn with the royal entourage
panels.action: At dawn on the south bank of the Musi, Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah on horseback surveys the misty plain, while attendants hold surveying instruments and mark the ground with stakes.

dialogue.text: By 1591, he chose the Musi’s southern bank. Ferishta records that the sultan resolved to found a new capital, moving his court from rugged Golconda to a planned city on open land.

i18n.hi: १५९१ तक उसने मूसी की दक्षिणी धार चुनी। फ़रिश्ता लिखता है कि सुल्तान ने नया राजधानी-शहर बसाने का निश्चय किया, दरबार को ऊबड़-खाबड़ गोलकोंडा से खुली ज़मीन पर बने नियोजित नगर में ले जाने का।

panels.shot: top-down view of a chalked cross on the earth where the four roads will meet
panels.action: Hands of surveyors draw a precise cross on the bare earth with chalk and stakes, marking four broad avenues that converge, while Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah stands at the center, looking down.

dialogue.text: At the heart he ordered four great roads to meet, a chauraha in stone. On this crossing, the Charminar would rise, its four minarets watching over the city’s intersecting paths.

i18n.hi: बीचोंबीच उसने चार बड़ी सड़कों को मिलाने का हुक्म दिया, पत्थर का एक चौरााहा। इसी मुकाम पर चारमीनार उठनी थी, जिसकी चार मीनारें शहर की कटती राहों पर नज़र रखेंगी।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of Muhammad Quli placing the foundation stone of Charminar
panels.action: In a solemn ceremony, Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah kneels to place a carved foundation stone as craftsmen and courtiers stand in respectful silence around the marked crossing.

dialogue.text: The Charminar’s own inscription fixes the moment: in 1591–92, Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah laid its foundations, naming himself its patron and anchoring his new Hyderabad in carved stucco and lime.

i18n.hi: चारमीनार की खुद की लिखत वक़्त तय करती है: १५९१–९२ में मुहम्मद क़ुली क़ुतुब शाह ने नींव डाली, खुद को सरपरस्त लिखा और अपने नए हैदराबाद को नक्काशदार चूने और गारे में बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: medium wide of artisans building Charminar amid busy construction of streets and bazaars
panels.action: Artisans haul stone blocks and carve arches on the rising Charminar, while beyond it workers lay straight, wide streets lined with arcaded shops and houses taking shape.

dialogue.text: Around the Charminar, avenues and bazaars spread in a planned grid. Hyderabad was not a fort-town grown by chance; it was a diagram of power and order drawn directly into earth.

i18n.hi: चारमीनार के चारों ओर चौड़ी सड़कें और बाज़ार जाली की तरह फैले। हैदराबाद कोई यूँ ही उगा क़िला-शहर नहीं; ये ज़मीन पर सीधे खींचा गया ताक़त और अनुशासन का नक़्शा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Muhammad Quli with Mir Momin and a court physician over another plan
panels.action: In a shaded hall, Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah listens as a senior advisor, identified by scholarly robes and a manuscript, gestures to a plan marking a hospital and gardens near the city center; a Unani physician stands by with a medical text.

dialogue.text: The city’s plan drew more than markets. With counselors like Mir Momin, he plotted a Dar-ul-Shifa, a house of healing, and formal gardens, folding care and pleasure into Hyderabad’s very layout.

i18n.hi: शहर के नक़्शे ने सिर्फ़ बाज़ार नहीं बुलाए। मीर मोमिन जैसे मशीरों के साथ उसने दारुल-शिफ़ा, यानी शिफ़ा-ख़ाना, और दस्तूरी बाग़ात सोचे, देखभाल और सरूर को हैदराबाद की रगों में ही बुन दिया।

panels.shot: interior wide of Dar-ul-Shifa courtyard with patients, physicians and Muhammad Quli visiting
panels.action: In the courtyard of the Dar-ul-Shifa, physicians in turbaned caps consult patients seated on mats, while a scribe copies a medical text; Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah walks through, pausing to speak with a doctor.

dialogue.text: Unani physicians like Abdullah Tabib wrote Tibb-i Farid under this patronage. Hospitals and manuals together show a court that saw medicine as statecraft, and health as part of its urban duty.

i18n.hi: अबदुल्ला तबीब जैसे यूनानी हकीमों ने इसी सरपरस्ती में तिब्ब-ए फ़रीद लिखा। अस्पताल और किताबें मिलकर एक ऐसे दरबार को दिखाती हैं जो तिब्ब को सियासत और सेहत को शहर की ज़िम्मेदारी समझता था।

panels.shot: long shot of Mecca Masjid foundation site near the Charminar, with stone slabs and workers
panels.action: Near the Charminar, workers align massive stone slabs and begin raising arches on a vast platform that will become the Mecca Masjid, while Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah oversees from a shaded pavilion.

dialogue.text: Close by, foundations were laid for the Mecca Masjid, envisioned as a great congregational mosque, and the Badshahi Ashurkhana, a Shia ceremonial hall, binding Hyderabad’s center to ritual and remembrance.

i18n.hi: पास ही मक्का मस्जिद की नींव पड़ी, जिसे बड़ी जामिया मस्जिद सोचा गया, और बादशाही आशूरख़ाना, शिया मातमी मन्ज़िल, जिसने हैदराबाद के दिल को रस्म और याद से बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of an artisan carving a foundation inscription while Muhammad Quli watches
panels.action: An artisan carefully chisels Naskh script lines into a foundation slab, while Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah watches, hands clasped behind his back, the Charminar’s arches rising in the background.

dialogue.text: The Charminar inscription names Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah and dates the work. Unlike later tales, it says nothing of romance; it records a ruler, a year and a monument at the crossing of four roads.

i18n.hi: चारमीनार की लिखत मुहम्मद क़ुली क़ुतुब शाह का नाम और तारीख़ दर्ज करती है। बाद की कहानियों के उलट, इसमें इश्क़ का ज़िक्र नहीं; बस एक बादशाह, एक साल और चार राहों के चौराहे पर उठते समारक की गवाही है।

panels.shot: dim interior with storytellers whispering, contrasted with Muhammad Quli reading quietly
panels.action: In a corner of a courtyard, commoners huddle as one gestures, animated, telling a romantic story; at a distance, Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah sits alone with a manuscript, detached from the gossip.

dialogue.text: Later centuries spun a different tale, of a Hindu beloved named Bhagmati and a city founded in her honour. Modern historians, reading the sparse contemporary record, find no trace of her in his time.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद एक और कहानी गढ़ी गई—एक हिन्दू महबूबा भगमती और उसके सम्मान में बसाया गया शहर। आज के इतिहासकार, कम दस्तावेज़ों को पढ़कर, उसके ज़माने में उसका कोई निशान नहीं पाते।

panels.shot: medium shot of a scholar pointing to the word 'Hyderabad' in a document while Muhammad Quli listens
panels.action: A court scribe indicates the word ‘Hyderabad’ on a freshly written farman, while Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah listens, a small Shia standard resting nearby as a subtle symbol.

dialogue.text: The very name Hyderabad is more plausibly tied by scholars to Hyder, an epithet of Imam Ali central to Qutb Shahi Shia devotion, than to any Bhagmati. Legend and inscription pull in different directions.

i18n.hi: विद्वानों को खुद नाम ‘हैदराबाद’ ज़्यादा मुमकिन लगता है कि क़ुतुब शाही शिया अकीदे के केंद्र ‘हैदर’, यानी इमाम अली की उपाधि से जुड़ा हो, न कि किसी भगमती से। दास्तान और लिखत दो दिशाओं में खींचते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of Muhammad Quli writing poetry at night by lamplight
panels.action: By lamplight in his private chamber, Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah leans over a low desk, reed pen poised, as he writes flowing Dakhni verses into a bound manuscript.

dialogue.text: At night the builder of streets turned poet. His Kulliyat, preserved today in Hyderabad, gathers a vast Dakhni divan, making him one of the earliest major urban voices in that language.

i18n.hi: रात को सड़कें बसाने वाला सुल्तान शायर बन जाता। उसकी ‘कुल्लियात’, जो आज हैदराबाद में महफ़ूज़ है, भारी दक़नी दीवान समेटे है, जो उसे उस ज़बान का शुरुआती बड़ा शहरी आवाज़ों में शामिल करती है।

panels.shot: wide interior of a mehfil where courtiers listen as a reciter sings his Dakhni ghazal
panels.action: In a richly carpeted hall, a reciter stands, singing a Dakhni ghazal from Muhammad Quli’s manuscript, while the sultan reclines among courtiers, eyes half-closed, listening intently.

dialogue.text: Where court Persian had long held pride of place, he wrote and patronized in Dakhni. His verses wove love, devotion and the texture of Hyderabad’s streets into a new, self-confident urban speech.

i18n.hi: जहाँ दरबार में फ़ारसी को बरसों से सरदारी थी, वहाँ उसने दक़नी में लिखा और उसे सरपरस्ती दी। उसकी ग़ज़लें मोहब्बत, अकीदा और हैदराबाद की गलियों का रंग मिलाकर एक नई, खुद-एतमादी शहरी बोली बुनती हैं।

panels.shot: sunset wide of completed Charminar with bustling Hyderabad around it and Muhammad Quli on a balcony
panels.action: At sunset, the completed Charminar towers above thronged bazaars, processions near the Ashurkhana, and people moving toward the Mecca Masjid and Dar-ul-Shifa, while Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah watches from a palace balcony.

dialogue.text: By the end of his reign in 1611, Hyderabad pulsed around its four-pillared heart—a network of markets, mosques, gardens and clinics that stitched belief, trade and care into one urban fabric.

i18n.hi: १६११ तक उसके दौर के अंत में हैदराबाद अपने चारस्तम्भी दिल के इर्द-गिर्द धड़क रहा था—बाज़ार, मस्जिदें, बाग़ और शिफ़ा-ख़ाने, जो यक़ीन, व्यापार और देखभाल को एक ही शहरी कपड़े में सिलते थे।

panels.shot: modern aerial view of Charminar and Mecca Masjid, subtly weathered, within the dense present-day city
panels.action: In a contemporary aerial vista, the weathered Charminar rises amid dense modern Hyderabad, with the Mecca Masjid beside it and crowded lanes radiating outward, scaffolds clinging to parts of the old stone.

dialogue.text: Today conservation reports warn of strain and decay in the Charminar and Mecca Masjid, yet the planned cross-roads and stone still hold, carrying Muhammad Quli’s design through centuries of traffic and change.

i18n.hi: आज हिफ़ाज़ती रिपोर्टें चारमीनार और मक्का मस्जिद में थकान और जर्जर पत्थर की चेतावनी देती हैं, फिर भी वही काटदार सड़कें और चट्टानें कायम हैं, मुहम्मद क़ुली की तदबीर को सदियों की आवाजाही और बदलाव के पार ढोते हुए।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of Muhammad Quli's eyes dissolving into a soft-focus view of people using hospital, mosque and market
panels.action: An extreme close-up of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah’s thoughtful eyes dissolves into a blended scene where ordinary people today move through a clinic, pray in a mosque, and trade in markets under the Charminar.

dialogue.text: His memory stands not only in arches and couplets, but in a city shaped so that roads lead as surely to healing and gathering as to power, reminding us that founding a capital can also be founding a care.

i18n.hi: उसकी याद सिर्फ़ मेहराबों और शेरों में नहीं, एक ऐसे शहर में भी है जिसे यूँ तराशा गया कि रास्ते जितने हुकूमत की तरफ़ जाते हैं, उतने ही शिफ़ा और जमघट की तरफ़, याद दिलाते हुए कि राजधानी बसाना, देखभाल बसाना भी हो सकता है।
